# Start with rdy

rdy holds what a person intends and decided. rdy computes. You write. The person decides.

Work through rdy's tools only. Never edit .rdy/, the working copy or the rendered site.
Never approve, tag or answer on your own judgment. Relay the person's exact words.

For every change:

1.  `rdy_session`: your own `agent:` actor, and a run named for the task.
2.  `rdy_brief` the blocks you will change.
3.  `rdy_write`, citing the briefing's token.
4.  Answer the consequences of each write.
5.  `rdy_suspects` and `rdy_tensions` on your view.
6.  `rdy_plan`: close or answer each item.
7.  `rdy_propose` with a title and a summary.
8.  Show the person the card and the live link, and relay their answer.

Keep to the rules you get here. Before you start a kind of work below for the first time in a task, load its ruleset: `rdy_instructions {load: ["rdy:<name>"]}`. Your person's and your project's rules follow, and they win where they differ, except for the rule on approvals above. When the person states a rule, load `rdy:write`, then save the rule with `rdy_rule`.

rows.text:
# Write and change content

Load this ruleset when you create or change content, structure, decisions or links.

## Using this guide

rdy delivers this guide through `rdy_instructions`. No file needs saving, and you download nothing. `rdy setup` writes three lines at the top of `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the project root, and they tell an agent to call `rdy_instructions`. It also creates the person's meta project if none exists. Outside a project, and in the meta project, it writes no stub.

It is for an agent that works on an rdy project for a person. rdy computes. You write. The person decides.

From Release 1, a tool, parameter, result field, code or config key changes only with an upgrade path in the same release. A renamed name keeps working, with a warning, for two minor releases and at least 30 days. Message and fix texts can change in any release, so match the code, never the text. After an update, read `rdy_schema` again.

## Agent instructions

At the start of every task, call `rdy_session` with your own actor and run, or state `rdy/actor` and `rdy/run` in `_meta`. Then call `rdy_instructions`. It returns every required rule in full, and a menu of the other rulesets. The bootstrap is rdy's one required built-in ruleset, and the rest of this guide is on the menu. CLI: `rdy instructions`. Until a call succeeds, `rdy_overview` and `rdy_brief` carry a reminder.

-   A menu entry is `{id, name, when, layer, required, tokens, hints}`. Read `name` and `when`, then load the rulesets that your task needs with `rdy_instructions {load: [ids]}`. rdy never picks for you, and `hints` are only hints.
-   Use the menu's id: `rdy:<name>`, `project:<doc-id>` or `person:<doc-id>`. `rdy:<name>` loads a built-in ruleset only, so a bare name such as `write` does not load one. A bare doc id that both layers hold fails with `E_BAD_INPUT`: use the layer-qualified id. An id that is not in the menu fails with `E_NOT_FOUND`.
-   To get every built-in ruleset whole, pass `full: true`. CLI: `rdy instructions --full`. Required rules of every layer still arrive. Stored optional rulesets still need `load`.
-   Each rule names its layer. The built-in `rdy` rules come first, then the project's, then the person's. When a person's rule and a project rule disagree, follow the person's. The built-in approval rule holds over both.
-   Follow the rules for the whole task. "Required" means that rdy always delivers the rule, not that rdy enforces it.
-   rdy gives only landed rules. A rule in a view or an open proposal is not in force yet.
-   A refused call gives no rules, never part of them. Do what its fix says, then call again. `E_VALIDATION` reads `<layer> source: <first issue>`. `E_LIMIT` names the bound that the call passed.
-   With no meta project, the person layer is empty, and `hint` names `rdy setup`, which creates one. Tell the person when it finishes.

**Writing a rule.** When the person states a rule, save it with one `rdy_rule` call, from any session: `rdy_rule {scope, op: "add", text: "<the rule>", why: "<one line>", evidence: "<the person's exact words>"}`. CLI: `rdy rule add`. If the person answered your question, pass that question as `question`. To change a rule, use `op: "edit"` with its `id`. To retire one, use `op: "remove"` with its `id`, and no `text`.

-   **Scope.** `person` is the person's meta project, for their preferences and their rules for all work. `project` is this project, for a rule specific to it. Ask the person only when you are unsure.
-   **Evidence.** Pass the person's exact words, never your own. Use `rdy_rule` only for a rule that the person stated. A subagent never relays, so a subagent never calls `rdy_rule`. rdy cannot check either rule.
-   **Wording.** When your `text` goes beyond the person's words, show it to the person before the call. After each landing, tell the person where the rule went and show all the saved wording, from `rule.text`: `Saved to your own rules, for all your projects: "<rule>".` If the place or the wording is wrong, the person says so, and you correct it the same way.
-   **Default place.** With no `ruleset`, the rule goes in `My rules` or `Project rules`. rdy creates these docs on first use, with `required: true`. With no `applies_to`, the selector is `all`.
-   **Rules for some work.** A required doc delivers every rule in it, so a narrower selector there is only a hint. It shows in the menu's `hints`, and the rule still arrives on every task. For a rule meant only for some work, pass `ruleset` with a named ruleset that is not required, and a narrower `applies_to`. A rule with `all` arrives on every task, wherever it is. Tell the person the ruleset's name. `rdy_rule` does not create a named ruleset (`E_NOT_FOUND`). Create it by the normal path below.
-   **Stops.** The reply can stop before the rule lands:

    -   `state: "card"`: the policy has `rules_from_chat: card`. Show the card as it is. Then relay the answer: `rdy_rule {scope, answer: {ref, option, card_hash, evidence, question}}`.
    -   `state: "not_ready"`: read `issues`, then finish the open proposal `ref` by the normal path. For `scope: "person"`, use a session on the meta project.
    -   `corrected.state: "normal_path"`: the change touches stable content (`E_BRIEF_REQUIRED`), or the rule's decision governs other blocks (`E_BAD_INPUT`). Brief `corrected.blocks` and use the normal path.
    -   `E_NO_PROJECT`: do what its fix says. With no meta project, the fix is `run rdy setup`.

**Writing a rule by the normal path.** Use this path for the stops above and for a named ruleset. For a rule that you inferred or want to suggest, ask the person first, or use this path and show the card. Record the rule as an `instruction` block under a doc or section, with a `decided_by` link to the decision that is its reason: `{"op":"create","type":"instruction","parent":"<doc>","body":"<the rule>","fields":{"applies_to":["all"]},"links":{"decided_by":[{"target":"D-…"}]}}`. Read `rdy_schema {block_type: "instruction"}` for its fields. CLI: `rdy new instruction`.

-   A selector is `all`, `area:<name>`, `type:<block type>` or `act:<act>`. A rule with `all`, or any rule in a doc with `required: true`, is required.
-   A named ruleset is a doc that holds `instruction` blocks. Leave `required` off. Its lead paragraph becomes the menu's `when`, so say there when to load it.
-   The person's own rules go in their meta project, `~/.rdy/meta` by default. Outside an rdy project, `rdy mcp` serves it.
-   Propose the rule like any change. It is in force after it lands.
-   Pass on `W_INSTRUCTION_SELECTOR`: the `area:` selector names an area that the pack lacks, so it matches nothing yet.

## Ground rules

-   The person talks to you in chat. You do the work through the rdy MCP tools, and you relay the person's decisions.
-   Don't ask the person to run routine rdy commands. The CLI is a fallback.
-   Use the tools only. Never edit files under `.rdy/`, the working copy, an export or the rendered site.
-   When you run the `rdy` CLI, set `RDY_ACTOR` to your own `agent:` actor on every call. Never run it as the person.
-   Never claim a `human:` actor. An agent session with one fails with `E_PERMISSION`. Relay the person's words instead.
-   When a command fails with `E_BAD_INPUT` because the configured `actor` is outside the actor form, tell the person. The fix names the file. Don't edit it yourself.
-   Never approve, tag or answer on your own judgment. Every one of those acts relays the person's own words.
-   rdy refuses a tag from an agent session unless it relays the person's words. See "Approvals and relays" in the `rdy:approvals` ruleset.
-   When an error says a store is open or locked, read the code. `E_LOCKED` means another process holds the store: stop that process or use the daemon. `E_HELD_BY_READER` means an earlier read state in this process holds it: release that state and try again.
-   "No suspects" means no stale pins. It does not mean that the content is correct.

## Structure first

When you start a project or a new area, plan the tree first: folders by area, a doc type for each doc, decisions recorded with `rdy_decide` and no parent, open questions as question blocks and terms in the glossary; show the person the plan before the first content write.

A flat list of pages is the most common failure. These details make the plan work:

-   Create a folder with `{"op":"create","type":"folder","fields":{"name":"billing","title":"Billing","description":"…"}}`. Don't use a name prefix such as `billing-overview` in place of a folder.
-   A doc or folder name uses only `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`. A name that reads as a block id fails with `E_BAD_NAME`. For `d-` and `fd-` ids, rdy ignores case. The refusal carries a fixed name in `corrected`.
-   Give every folder a one-sentence `description`, and open every doc with a plain lead paragraph.
-   Use the `page` doc type only when no other type fits. One topic per doc: split a long doc into sections, not into sibling docs.
-   A question's `prompt` states the product question and its options. Put your own advice in chat.
-   Close a question with a decision that has an `answers` link to it. Never write the answer into the question.
-   Define each term as a `term` block in the doc that explains it. The site's glossary page collects them.
-   To fix a flat project, create the folders, then move each doc with a `move` op. A move keeps block ids and history.

## The loop, for every change

1.  **Start.** Call `rdy_session` with your own `agent:` actor, a `run` named for the task, and role `writer`. Keep the run name when you resume. See "Actors and runs" in `rdy:troubleshoot` for the form of each. Then call `rdy_instructions`, as "Agent instructions" says.
2.  **Brief.** Call `rdy_brief` on the blocks you will change, or on a doc with `path`. To brief one section, pass `<doc>#<heading-slug>`. To create a block, brief its parent. Read `governs`: "Decisions and their links" says what to check when you change a block's text.
3.  **Write.** Pass the briefing's `base.token` string as `brief`, not the whole briefing. An `E_BRIEF_REQUIRED` or `E_BRIEF_STALE` reply carries a fresh briefing: retry with its `base.token`.
4.  **Answer the consequences** of each write, as "What each consequence asks" in `rdy:after-write` says. Brief again before each follow-up write.
5.  **Check.** After your last write, run `rdy_suspects` and `rdy_tensions` with `scope` set to your view. Clear what your changes caused.
6.  **Plan.** Read `rdy_plan` for your view. Close or answer each item, as "Change plans" in `rdy:after-write` says.
7.  **Propose.** Call `rdy_propose` with a plain-words `title` and a `summary`. A version without a summary gets no card: `rdy_pending` lists it under `not_ready`.
8.  **Land or ask.** When `ready` is false, fix each issue and propose again. When `policy.verdict` is `accepts`, land with `rdy_land`. Otherwise relay the card, as "Approvals and relays" in `rdy:approvals` says.

Propose once per iteration, at the break that `propose.cadence` sets. Propose again only when the view changed since the last version.

To see what your view changes before you propose, call `rdy_diff {from: "view:<run>"}`. See "Reading changes" in the `rdy:read` ruleset.

-   Brief before editing (`rdy_brief`); writes to stable content must cite a briefing (`brief: <token>`).
-   Before editing a block, read it with format markdown or yaml: compact lines are a summary.
-   Work in your own view; include others' changes, never write into their views.
-   When a block comes back as a consequence a second time in a session, do not rewrite it again: confirm it (repin) or ask the person, and show what remains as a change plan.

## Decisions and their links

-   `decided_by` is a link you write on a content block: this decision governs the block.
-   When you change what a block says, read its `decided_by` and `implements` links against the new text, on an `editorial` write too. Add the decision that the text now rests on. Remove a link that the text no longer rests on. A wrong link gives the block a wrong as-built status and a wrong "Why?" trail. rdy cannot judge this for you.
-   `implements` on `rdy_write` says that the change carries out these decisions. rdy adds an `implements` link to every block that the write creates or edits. It skips decisions, questions, findings, sources, docs, folders and sections, but not notes.
-   So group writes by each block's own governing decisions. Name only the decisions that the new text carries out, not every old link. Never pass a whole list of decisions on one write. Write scaffolding and planned notes in their own write.
-   A write takes one justification: `implements`, `editorial: {class, reason}` or `reflects`. The editorial class is `typo`, `restructure` or `clarify`. "Sources, findings and code" in `rdy:as-built` explains `reflects`.
-   The approval card's Justification fact shows each claim, such as `implements D-…` or `editorial clarify: <reason>`.
-   An accepted decision is frozen (`E_FROZEN`). Only its tracking fields change, such as a disposition, and each such edit needs `editorial`.
-   An update replaces only the link kinds it names, and `"<kind>": []` removes that kind. Read the block first, and send the full list for each kind you name.
-   `$name` placeholders work only inside one write, also as `{{$name}}` in text. The create must come before every op that names it.
-   Keep a chain of creates that name each other in one write. When you must split creates across writes, replace each placeholder with the real id of the block already written. Group by each block's own decisions even in a recovery write.
-   New blocks that name each other in text (a cycle) need two writes. Create them with the references left out, then update the text with the real ids.
-   Give each decision a `title` (80 characters or fewer) and a `why` (160 or fewer). Card option labels take 60 or fewer.
-   A question's `recommended` is the exact text of one option, never `o1`. A wrong form only warns (`W_CARD_WORDS`). `rdy_answer` still takes option ids such as `o1`.
-   Give every recommendation a reason: `recommend_reason` on a question, and `recommend` with `recommend_reason` on a decision. `recommend` takes only `confirm` or `reject`. Write it in one line of 200 characters or fewer. rdy warns when it is missing or long.
-   Add a new block's `affects` and `describes` links in the write that creates it. A later link-only edit makes every pin on the block go stale. Still remove a wrong link.
-   Before you supersede, count the blocks in the briefing's `dependents`. If only the reason changes, refine instead, or supersede with `part`.
-   After a supersede, move each citing block's links to the new decision yourself.
-   For a process ruling that no content carries, pass `fields: {needs_content: false}`. Otherwise the card shows the decision as an exception.
-   Before you choose a decision key, look it up with `rdy_search` and check for an exact match. Never pick one from an export.
-   `authority_basis` is `direct_ruling`, `recorded_ruling`, `delegated`, `precedent`, `elimination` or `none`. A `delegated` decision needs `attested_by`, which names who ruled and under whose mandate.
-   `decided_at`, `recorded_at`, `effective_from` and `review_by` take an RFC 3339 UTC time, such as `2026-10-21T15:10:58Z`, or a date, such as `2026-10-05`.

**Briefing a new decision.** `rdy_decide`, `rdy_supersede` and `rdy_revoke` each create a decision under a parent. The parent is the doc, section or folder in `parent`. When you leave `parent` out, it is the project's decision home, or the project root when the project names none. `rdy_schema` names the decision home.

-   Brief that parent. A briefing of the old decision does not cover it.
-   `rdy_decide` and `rdy_revoke` take the token as `brief`. `rdy_supersede` takes it inside `decision`, as `decision.brief`.
-   The `E_BRIEF_REQUIRED` refusal names the parent, as `<id> (the parent of the new decision)`. It carries a fresh briefing: retry with its token.

-   `rdy_decide` takes its own parameters. It has no `message` and no `supersedes`. To supersede, use `rdy_supersede`.

-   When the person states something that should hold, record it at once with `rdy_decide` as a proposed decision, in their words, and say so in one line.
-   A decision is worth recording when every agent should keep to it next month; a passing preference is not.
-   Record a decision with `rdy_decide` and no parent: it goes to the decision home, or to the project root when the project names none; link content to it with `decided_by`, and never put a decision in a content doc or create a doc to hold decisions.
-   When a change retires only some of a decision's rules, supersede that part (`rdy_supersede` with `part`), not the whole decision.
-   While coding, a change within the design is just code; a gap is a proposed decision plus the doc update; a contradiction is a finding plus a superseding decision, and you stop when it is blocking or `one_way`.

## Links and Grounded

Grounded measures how well content ties to what it is about. It checks mentions only on normative blocks, such as requirements, constraints and claims.

-   Tie each content block to what it is about. A block with no tie gets the check `untied_content`.
-   Link each entity that a normative block names. An unlinked mention there counts against Grounded. When the mention is only in passing, dismiss it with `rdy_resolve` and a reason.
-   On prose, notes and other informative blocks, an unlinked mention is only a link suggestion. It adds no check. Accept the suggestion when the block is about that entity. Ignore a passing mention.
-   An entity with `everyday: true` gets no link suggestions anywhere.
-   Don't add links only to raise the score.

-   Search a thing's name, key or alias with `rdy_search` to get its fact sheet.
-   Write responses carry suggestions (links to the entities your text names, new entities for literals that recur): accept the right ones with one `rdy_accept` call; they never block.
-   Fact sheets, search hits and briefings carry a confidence level: act on high; on medium or low, widen the search, fix the coverage issues you can, or ask the person before you act.
-   Link every entity a normative statement names, and elsewhere the entities a block is about; dismiss a passing mention of an everyday word with `rdy_resolve` (mention, dismiss).

New assessments use method 2. A stored method-1 assessment keeps its old scores, so the same content can score differently in an older version. Don't compare scores across methods. A score that rises with the move to method 2 shows a new method, not better docs. Never tell the person that their docs improved because of it.

## Hygiene

-   Stop at the first failed write. Read the view before you run anything again.
-   Change each block at most once per write. To edit and move a block, use one `update` op with `move_to`.
-   When a decision narrows or reverses a rule, find every statement of the old rule. Search its words, and search with `governed_by`.
-   Before you propose, read each section that you changed from top to bottom. Two blocks on one page must not contradict.
-   Before you propose a decision, read its related decisions and the neighbours in its section. Search for closed lists that it changes.
-   When a block states an exception, link it to the block that states the rule.
-   Search the terms (`rdy_search`, `types` set to `term`) before you introduce a term or a field name.
-   Before you remove or move a doc, brief it and read each block in `dependents`.
-   Don't write decisions that sit in a sibling view's open proposal.
-   A list of ids in a hand-off names the project that holds each id. Read an id only in its own project.
-   Quote decisions from `rdy_read`, not from the site or an export.
-   When you retitle a doc, decide its `name` too, because the name sets its page path.

-   To show a ref as plain text, put a backslash before its two opening braces. Without it, rdy reads the text as a ref, and a ref to no block fails with `E_UNKNOWN_REF`.

rows.text:
# After a write

Load this ruleset when you handle consequences, re-affirmations, change plans or readiness.

## What each consequence asks

Each entry names a `block`, a `kind`, `because` and a `follow_up`. Its `id` (`cq-…`) also names a plan item in a plan answer. Follow its `fix` when it has one.

-   `update`: rewrite the block so that it agrees with the change.
-   `confirm`: read the block. If it still holds, repin it. Some `confirm` entries need no repin, and their `fix` says so. Answer each of those as a plan item instead.
-   `reaffirm`: an accepted decision is suspect on the changed block. If it still holds, re-affirm it. Otherwise supersede it.
-   `resolve`: for a tension, see "Tensions". For a conflict, write the block from the version you want.

Conflicts are recorded, not errors: resolve one by writing the block.

An accepted decision gets `reaffirm` only when it is suspect on the cause. Any other reach of an accepted decision gives `confirm`, such as a refine's reach, a `describes` link or a premise with no pin. That `confirm` needs no repin: check the decision, and supersede it if it no longer holds. A decision's own `affects` link to the changed block gives no entry.

`already_written: true` names a block that your view already wrote. Check it, then act on its `follow_up`.

A supersede or revoke lists each dependent block, also one that reaches the old decision through `implements`. `because.edges` names every link. When the dependent states a literal that the change removed, the follow-up is `update`. `because.values` lists the removed literals, and `matched` lists the lines that state one. Edit those lines. With no match the follow-up is `confirm`, and a refine or a part supersede is always `confirm`. rdy reads only the first 16 KiB of a dependent, so a cut text gets `update`: read the whole block yourself. rdy matches literals exactly, so search for copies in other forms yourself.

A change to a source gives an entry on each block that reflects it. A change to a finding gives an entry on each decision that depends on it.

**Repins.** Read every suspect block before you repin it: a repin claims that the block still holds. Repin in a separate write, after the write that changes the target. A repin cannot clear a suspect on a deleted, superseded or revoked target. Point the link at the decision in force instead.

A repin of an accepted or rejected decision fails with `E_FROZEN`. In a repin batch, skip those decisions. Re-affirm a suspect accepted decision instead.

**Suspects in a view.** A changed target shows in `rdy_suspects` for your view. A supersede or revoke in a view raises no `superseded` suspect there. It comes only as a write consequence, so act on it then. A suspect with `deferred` carries a deferral that a person accepted.

## Re-affirming a decision

A re-affirmation records that a suspect accepted decision still holds. The decision keeps its ruling, body and links.

-   Write `{"op":"reaffirm","id":"D-…","reason":"…"}` in `rdy_write`. The reason takes 1 to 2000 characters.
-   To re-affirm every decision in your view that is suspect on one block, pass `because` with that block in place of `id`.
-   `targets` limits the op to the suspects on those blocks. `base` goes with `id` only.
-   Brief the decisions you re-affirm, as for any write.
-   A re-affirmation also clears a suspect on a superseded, revoked or deleted target, which a repin cannot.
-   The CLI fallback is `rdy reaffirm <id>... --reason "<text>"`, or `--because <id>`.

Edit blocks in place, then re-affirm the affected decisions in your view before you propose. Never create new blocks to avoid re-affirm cards.

The person can also re-affirm on a `reaffirm` card in `rdy_pending`. See "Approvals and relays" in the `rdy:approvals` ruleset.

## Change plans

Every proposal carries a change plan: the to-do list that its change to canon leaves. rdy computes the items, and nobody writes them. `rdy_plan` reads your view's plan. Pass `proposal`, `landing` or `decision` to read another plan.

Write with `rdy_write`; propose with `rdy_propose`. Before proposing, read `rdy_plan` and close or defer each item. Give every deferral a reason. Re-affirm a suspect decision that still holds with a `reaffirm` op, and supersede one that does not.

Item kinds, and what each takes:

Table 1

| Kind | Closes by itself when the version | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update` | changes or deletes the block | `defer` |
| `rejustify` | removes every link to the retired target | `defer` |
| `reaffirm` | re-affirms, supersedes or revokes the decision | `defer` |
| `confirm` | repins the block | `confirm` or `defer` |
| `update_implementation` | is followed by a commit that touches the file and cites the cause or a decision of this version | `done` or `defer` |
| `tension` (`tn-…`) | — | `confirm` or `dismiss` |

A `tension` item asks you to answer an advisory tension of the version. `confirm` accepts it as it is, and `dismiss` says that it does not apply.

-   Answer with `rdy_plan {answers: [{item, act, reason}]}`. `item` is a `pi-` id, a unique prefix of one, a `tn-` id or a `cq-` id.
-   `confirm`, `defer` and `dismiss` need a reason. `done` keeps none.
-   rdy checks all the answers first, then records all of them or none.
-   `rdy_propose` takes the same list as `plan_answers`, recorded in the same batch as the proposal.
-   An answer lapses when the block or the cause changes (`W_PLAN_ANSWER_LAPSED`). Answer the item again.
-   The person accepts or refuses deferrals on the version's `defer` card. Approval waits for that answer (`E_DEFERRAL_OPEN`).
-   An `update_implementation` item never blocks, and its deferral needs no card.
-   On stable content, an open item other than a code item makes the version not ready (`E_PLAN_OPEN`). On drafts it warns (`W_PLAN_OPEN`). An unanswered tension item makes the version not ready on drafts too.
-   The CLI fallback is `rdy plan`, and `rdy plan confirm|defer|done|dismiss <item>... --reason "<text>"`.

**Group answers.** In `rdy_plan`, an answer can name `group: {kind?, follow_up?, doc?, edge?}` in place of `item`. Give at least one field. The act answers every open item that matches each field you give.

-   Add `repin: true` to a `confirm` group to repin each matched block in the same call. On stable content, that repin needs `implements`, `editorial` or `reflects`, as `rdy_write` takes them.
-   Read every block in the group before you confirm it. A group answer claims each of them, as a repin does.
-   The CLI takes the same fields as flags: `--kind`, `--follow-up`, `--doc`, `--edge` and `--repin`.

Close an item with real work when you can. Defer only what needs a separate proposal, and say why.

-   Prefer the edit to a `defer` on an `update` item. A deferral needs the person's answer on a `defer` card. A repin never closes an `update` item.

## Readiness

rdy checks a version when it makes it, not only when it lands. The propose reply gives `ready` and `issues`. Each issue names one failed check, with its own code and fix. A version that is not ready gets no approve card, and `rdy_pending` lists it under `not_ready`.

The checks include these:

-   No conflict is unresolved, and no blocking tension would land.
-   Each change that touches stable content records a briefing.
-   No item on stable content other than a code item is open, and each tension item has an answer (`E_PLAN_OPEN`).
-   No `blocking` pack rule fails on stable content (`E_RULE_CHECK`).
-   A choice from an alternative set names one decision for its options (`E_ALT_DECISION`).
-   With `coverage.gate: no_lower`, the version lowers the coverage of no page and of the corpus (`E_COVERAGE_LOWERED`). Call `rdy_coverage` to see what lowered it, then link the new content to what it describes.

Fix each issue, then propose again.

rdy stores the result as the version's assessment. After approval, a landing checks freshness and later refusals. Freshness fails when the version is no longer the latest, a landing since its base changed a block in its reach or a key that it writes, or the authority policy changed.

-   On `E_PROPOSAL_MOVED` with a card in `corrected`, show it and ask again.
-   A competing landing can shift a key that the version writes, such as to a `-2` suffix. Landing then refuses once with `E_PROPOSAL_MOVED`, and the fresh card names the new key in its Keys fact. Show that card and ask again. With no Keys fact, every key lands as written.
-   On `E_PROPOSAL_MOVED` with `issues` and no card, fix each issue and propose again.
-   On `E_PROPOSAL_NOT_READY`, fix each issue and propose again.

Pack rules also run on each write. An advisory rule that fails, or a blocking rule that fails outside stable content, warns with `W_RULE_CHECK`. Follow its fix. A blocking rule that fails on stable content shows `E_RULE_CHECK` in `on_change`. The write still succeeds. Fix it before you propose.

`W_PACK_SEVERITY` says that the pack lowers `unjustified_change` in stable content. rdy keeps it blocking. Tell the person.

## Tensions

Tensions: `rdy_tensions` lists disagreements between changes and with canon; resolve one with a change, or dismiss it with `rdy_resolve` and a reason; a blocking one refuses a landing that has a side in it and would put every side into canon.

-   Resolve a tension with a change: edit or repin a side. A `semantic` tension resolves only when a side's text changes.
-   For an `unjustified_change`, rewrite the block with `implements`, `editorial` or `reflects`.
-   Dismiss a tension only when it needs no action: `rdy_resolve {tension, dismiss: {reason}}`. A blocking one needs the reviewer role or the person, as another actor than every side's author.
-   To relay the person's dismissal, add their `evidence` and your `question` to `dismiss`.
-   Sibling views forked from one parent see each other's edits as blocking `premise_shift` tensions. They clear when the views are included into one view and repinned.

rulesets.title: After a write
rulesets.when: handle consequences, re-affirmations, change plans or readiness

rulesets.name: approvals

rows.text:
# Approvals, policy and disputes

Load this ruleset when you show a card, relay an answer, or work under the authority policy or a dispute.

## Approvals and relays

-   At session start, also call `rdy_pending` and tell the person in one line what waits; do not list it unless asked.
-   Propose at the point `rdy_session`'s `propose.cadence` sets, by default at a natural break; under changes, propose when a write reply says `propose_due`.
-   Present a batch card from `rdy_pending` at the end of an iteration, then each exception on its own; show each option label word for word and never change the options, the recommendation or the version.
-   Relay the person's answer with `rdy_answer`: pass the `card_hash` you showed, their words as evidence and your question; interrupt the person only for a blocking item.
-   Use `rdy_answer` with `elicit: true` to ask a supporting client to show the card. Never send a request to `/~ui/`. Use `rdy_answer`, with elicitation or the person's relayed words.
-   When `rdy_propose` reports policy accepts, land with `rdy_land`; else show the card to the person.

Before you ask for an approval, check the propose reply: `ready` is true, `blocking` is empty, and no tension has `refuses: true`. Give the person the live link: `rdy_site {scope: "proposal:P-x@n"}`. When the proposal changes a publication profile, add `profile` to that call. Then the person reviews the selection they will publish. Pass on every warning in the reply.

Relay each card in this order:

1.  Call `rdy_pending` with your `session_ref`. Find the approve card for your version, and the `confirm` and `defer` cards beside it.
2.  Show each card to the person word for word, with the option labels as rdy gives them. Keep the `recommended` mark and the line `Why recommended: <reason>`. The approve card counts exceptions but does not show them, so show each exception card too.
3.  Relay each card beside the batch first. An approval waits until every exception has a `confirm` answer (`E_EXCEPTION_OPEN`) and the `defer` card has an answer (`E_DEFERRAL_OPEN`). Accepting the deferrals changes the approve card's hash. Call `rdy_pending` again, and show the fresh approve card.
4.  Call `rdy_answer {ref, option, card_hash, evidence, question, session_ref, kind: "card"}`. `evidence` is a string, not an object. It holds their exact words, such as the label they chose.

**Elicitation.** When your client supports form elicitation, call `rdy_answer {ref, card_hash, elicit: true}` in place of steps 2 to 4. The client shows rdy's own card, and the person's choice goes straight to rdy. A decline or cancel records nothing. On `E_ELICITATION_UNAVAILABLE`, show the card in chat and relay the answer with `option` and `evidence`.

The live site also shows the person's pending cards at `/~ui/`. That page is for the person. Never send a request to it.

-   Relay only the person's exact words. Never approve, confirm or reject for them, and never fill a gap with your guess.
-   `option` is the option id from the card (`approve`, `confirm`, `reject`, `o1`), not its label.
-   The recommended option has `recommended: true` and a `reason` (200 characters or fewer). No other option has either.
-   An approve card's reason is one of three fixed texts. Don't rewrite it.
-   The approve card's facts include Justification, Re-affirms and Change plan. Show them as rdy gives them.
-   The approve card and each decision's `confirm` card have a Related decisions fact. It lists the decisions found by a link. It only counts the rows found by text, as in `2 listed by link, 14 found by text, 0 omitted: …`. A card that an older rdy stored can still list text rows. To read the text rows, use the briefing or the fact sheet.
-   A re-affirmation of a `one_way` decision is an exception with its own `confirm` card. Other re-affirmations are listed in Re-affirms.
-   Branch on the card kind. Send `confirm` only to a `confirm` card. A tension card offers `dismiss` and `later`. Never send one option name to every card.
-   A `defer` card (`defer:P-x@n`) offers `o1` "Accept the deferrals", `o2` "Refuse: do them in this proposal" and `later`. A refusal makes the version not ready.
-   A `reaffirm` card (`reaffirm:<block>@<version>`) offers `o1` "They still hold" and `o2` "Keep them suspect". `o1` lands the re-affirmation at once. `o2` needs the person's reason in `note`.
-   `defer` and `reaffirm` cards carry no recommended option. Show both options and wait for the person's own choice.
-   A decision that no content applies is an exception, and it needs its own `confirm`.
-   A decision that only structural blocks carry, such as a publication profile, a folder or a doc, always reads as applied by no content. Show its exception card before the approve card.
-   Before you report a landing, check it: read `landing` in the answer, or `rdy_log`. When another landing comes between your propose and your relay, the base moves and rdy refuses the relay. Stop at the first refusal, show the fresh card and ask again.
-   A changed card is refused with the fresh card in `corrected`, as are `E_PROPOSAL_MOVED` and `E_ITEM_MOVED`. Show it and ask again.
-   An approving answer to a version that is not ready fails with `E_PROPOSAL_NOT_READY`. The message counts the problems, such as `P-x@n is not ready: 2 issues`. Each entry in `issues` names one failed check, with its own code and fix. Fix each issue, propose again, and relay the new card.
-   Pass `all_recommended` (a list of `{ref, card_hash}`) only when the person asks you to accept every recommendation. It refuses `defer` and `reaffirm` cards.
-   A relay checks the question in your view. A view that moved a question cannot relay its answer: relay from a fresh view.
-   Relay only from the session the person talks to. A subagent never relays.
-   A tag is the person's act too: `rdy_tag {version, evidence, question}`, on their words.
-   The CLI fallbacks are `rdy answer <ref> <option> --card <hash>` and `rdy approve P-x@n`. Add `--relayed-by <your actor> --evidence "<their words>" --question "<what you asked>"`. `--relayed-by` takes your actor alone, without a run. The run comes from your session.

## The authority policy

The authority policy is an `authority_policy` block (`ap-…`) that a person approves. Its `agent_may_accept` rules say which versions an agent may land without a person. With no policy block, nothing lands without a person.

-   `rdy_policy {op: "init", doc}` starts it. It writes a proposed decision and the policy block from rdy's template into your view, and proposes them. The template accepts nothing. A person adds the rules, and each rule change implements a decision.
-   The propose reply and the approve card show the verdict as `Policy`. When it accepts, land with `rdy_land {proposal: "P-x@n"}`. CLI: `rdy land P-x@n`.
-   `E_POLICY_HUMAN` means the policy needs a person for this version, or your actor matches none of the rule's actors. Show the card and relay the answer.
-   The policy never accepts a version that is not ready, carries a redaction request, changes the policy, has an exception, defers an item that is not a code item, records a `direct_ruling` or `recorded_ruling` decision, makes a doc stable, or carries an imported decision status.
-   A landing under the policy records the policy version and is never signed.
-   Never edit the policy unless the person asks. A version that changes it always needs a person.

## Disputes

A person disputes a landing that they think is wrong, most often a wrong relay. A dispute shows on the landing and never blocks one.

-   Open and resolve are the person's acts. Relay their words: `rdy_dispute {op: "open", landing, reason, evidence, question}`.
-   `{op: "resolve", dispute, outcome, evidence, question}` takes `upheld`, `dismissed` or `withdrawn`. Only the person who opened a dispute withdraws it. Only `upheld` may name a correcting landing in `correction`.
-   `{op: "list", landing?, open?}` lists disputes, oldest first.
-   CLI: `rdy dispute open|resolve|list`, with `--relayed-by`, `--evidence` and `--question` for a relay.

rulesets.title: Approvals, policy and disputes
rulesets.when: show a card, relay an answer, or work under the authority policy or a dispute

rulesets.name: as-built

rows.text:
# As-built status and sources

Load this ruleset when you ship work, or set `built`, sources or code links.

## As-built status

Each decision has a `built` field: `planned`, the first release version that ships it, such as `0.41.0`, or `none` for a ruling that needs no content. A new decision starts `planned`, or `none` when it has `needs_content: false`. A content block takes its status from the decisions it cites through `decided_by` or `implements`: planned, since a version, or unversioned. `rdy_read`, `rdy_context`, briefings and `rdy show` show it. A public publication hides planned content.

-   Write content for a decision that is not built yet. It stays planned, and public renders hide it until the decision is built.
-   When the work ships, set `built` on the decision to the release version. Do it in the docs round after the merge, in the same write that turns the planned text into built text. `built` is a tracking field: on an accepted decision, the edit needs `editorial`.
-   Set a block's own `planned: true` or `since: <version>` only when its decisions give it the wrong status. While the override disagrees with them, writes and `rdy show` give `W_AS_BUILT_OVERRIDE`. Remove the override, or confirm its as-built plan item (edge `built`) with a reason. After the confirm lands, the warning stops until the override or the decisions' `built` changes.
-   Before a release, run `rdy_publication_check {profile, release: "<version>"}` (CLI: `--release`). `blocked` means that shown content or a shown decision ships in a later version, or that shown content refers to hidden planned content. Fix each one before the tag: set the right `built`, or hide the content.

**What does not show the status.** Read the block when you need its status.

-   `rdy_query` rows carry no as-built status.
-   The plain-text `rdy brief` shows neither the status nor `W_AS_BUILT_OVERRIDE`. Use `rdy brief --json` or `rdy show`.
-   A briefing leaves out `as_built` on an unversioned block. `rdy_read` and `rdy_context` keep it.
-   A profile with `planned: mark` shows planned blocks, and the release check does not count them. On an `org` profile, a reference to hidden planned content only warns.
-   An `instruction` block takes `planned` and `since`, but `rdy_instructions` delivers every landed instruction, whatever its status.

## Sources, findings and code

A `source` block (`S-…`) names a release, commit or spec. Its fields are `title`, `kind` (`release`, `commit` or `spec`), `locator` and an optional `version`. A `finding` block (`F-…`) states what surfaced, in `statement`, with 1 to 20 `evidence` entries.

Finding: record what surfaced with `rdy_write`, type finding, statement and 1 to 20 evidence entries; cite it from a decision with `depends_on`.

-   An evidence entry is `{quote, session_ref?, question?}` or `{source: "{{S-…}}"}`. Each value takes 1 to 2000 characters.
-   Findings and sources go to the decision home unless you pass `parent`. CLI: `rdy new finding` and `rdy new source`.
-   A decision cites its finding with a `depends_on` link. A superseding decision's exception card lists those findings in a Findings fact.
-   A finding is never deleted. Update it, or record a new finding.

**The** **`reflects`** **justification.** Use it for a change that follows a source or the code, not a decision. Pass `reflects: {sources: [...], code: true}` on `rdy_write`, with at least one of the two.

-   Never pass `reflects` with `implements` or `editorial`.
-   rdy adds a `reflects` link from each written content block to each source. The source must be in your view, or created in the same write. Otherwise rdy refuses the write with `E_BAD_INPUT`.
-   A source created in the same write counts, by its `$name`.
-   `code: true` records the code state of each written block that declares `reflects` globs. rdy refuses it when no written block declares them. `code: false` is refused: leave `code` out instead.
-   CLI: `rdy commit --reflects <source>` and `--reflects-code`. `rdy edit` takes the same flags.

**Code suspects.** A block's `reflects` field lists globs of the code files that it describes. When those committed files change, `rdy_suspects` shows a `code_changed` row for the block.

-   Read the code, fix the block if it no longer agrees, then repin with `{"op":"repin","id":"…","code":true}`. CLI: `rdy repin <id> --code`.
-   `rdy_brief {code_path}` lists the blocks whose globs match a file.
-   With no linked checkout, rdy records no code state and warns with `W_REFLECTS_NO_CODE`. Tell the person.

rulesets.title: As-built status and sources
rulesets.when: ship work, or set `built`, sources or code links

rulesets.name: read

rows.text:
# Read why and what changed

Load this ruleset when you explain why a block says something, or read changes.

## Why a block says what it says

Why: to learn why a block says what it says, call `rdy_trace`.

`rdy_trace {id}` explains a block. It lists the governing decisions, the sources it reflects, lineage, premises and questions. It also gives the landing that introduced the block, the landings that accepted each decision, and the plans those landings sealed.

-   `depth` takes 1 to 8 (default 3). `max_tokens` defaults to 1000. `detail: true` adds the recorded evidence.
-   `frontier` lists the decisions the reply did not expand: at the depth limit, or left out by a cut. To go on, call `rdy_trace` again and pass a `frontier` id as `id`.
-   `ungrounded: true` marks a stable normative block with no governing decision, no source and no `reflects` globs.
-   CLI: `rdy trace <id>`. The CLI reads canon by default, and the tool reads your view.

Governing includes the live decisions that affect an entity the block describes. A briefing's `governs` also lists proposed decisions, and `through` names the entity. A briefing adds `sources` and, for a decision, the `findings` it depends on. A briefing guards a write. Use `rdy_trace` for the reasons.

**Neighbors.** A briefing also lists `neighbors`: the content blocks that share a section or an entity with each covered block, same doc first. Read them before you write, because a link does not always join two blocks that must agree. `neighbors_by_doc` counts the full list on every page. Page with `next` until it is absent.

**Source existence.** Each source in a briefing has `existence`: `found`, `missing` or `unchecked`. It says whether rdy found the release or commit in a linked checkout. On `missing`, check the source's `locator` and tell the person.

## Reading changes

-   `rdy_diff {from, to?, doc?, detail?}` compares two scopes block by block. With only `from`, rdy picks the other side: a view diffs from its base, `tag:` or `landing:` diffs to canon, and `proposal:P-x@n` diffs from the version's base. `doc` limits it to one doc or folder. `detail: true` adds field values and word-level body diffs. CLI: `rdy diff <from> [<to>]`.
-   `rdy_log {landing}` reads one landing: its row and its change list. CLI: `rdy show landing:<id>`.
-   `rdy_read` takes `scope: "proposal:P-x@n"` and `scope: "landing:<id>"` to read a version or a past landing.
-   `rdy_query {filter}` selects blocks by fields and links, such as `type = decision and status = live and no in implements`. `rdy_schema` gives the grammar under `filter`, and a parse error names the column. CLI: `rdy q "<filter>"`. Use `rdy_search` to find text.
-   Each of them pages: a cut reply carries `next`. Pass it as `page` with the same request.

## The inbox

Read `rdy_inbox` at session start and when `rdy://inbox` changes, and ack what you have handled; notifications are best effort, the inbox is reliable.

Show the person their inbox with `rdy_inbox {person: true}`. Ack it only after they have seen it. Your own cursor belongs to your actor and run, and a new run starts at the log head.

rulesets.title: Read why and what changed
rulesets.when: explain why a block says something, or read changes

rulesets.name: publish

rows.text:
# Publications and the hub

Load this ruleset when you check or publish a profile, or use a hub.

## Publications

-   A publication profile is a `publication_profile` block under a doc. It has a `key`, a `title`, an `audience` (`org` or `public`) and a `select` list of doc and folder ids. `rdy new profile` creates one.
-   Propose, land and tag a profile like any block.
-   `rdy_publication_check {profile, scope?, against?}` checks the selection and the refs that leave it. Pass `against` to see what the output newly discloses.
-   A ref in the text of a selected block to a block outside the selection, or to no block, blocks a `public` profile and warns on an `org` one. Show the person every row and warning. The check authorizes nothing.
-   A link to a target outside the selection, such as `implements`, `decided_by` or `describes`, never changes the status, because no output shows it. The report lists these links apart in `references.links_outside` (CLI: `Links outside selection: <n>.`). Keep them: never remove a link to clear the check.
-   A ref by id to a decision outside the selection does not count either. A profiled output shows its display words, or nothing. So when a sentence needs the words, give the ref display words. A ref to a decision id that is no block still counts as missing.

**Profiles on the live site.** Call `rdy_site {profile}` with an optional `scope`. `profile` is an id, a key or `implicit:org`. CLI: `rdy site --profile <profile>`.

-   For a separate site that shows only that profile, call `rdy_site {profile, only: true}`. The scope must be canon: otherwise `E_BAD_INPUT`. CLI: `rdy serve --profile <profile>`.
-   On `E_SITE`, follow the fix in the message.
-   Pass on `W_SITE_PROFILE`. It says a profile-only site is open, or its profile is no longer in canon.
-   A `public` profile that has blocked references still serves on the live site, with a warning. It is not publishable. Run the check before any publish.

**Publish.** Call `rdy_publish {tag, to, site, keep_latest?}`. CLI: `rdy publish <tag> --to <remote> --site <site>`.

-   `to` names a remote in `publish` mode. The hub `site` selects the profile: don't pass one.
-   Sign in first. Tag the profile and the content first.
-   The call creates a candidate on the hub and publishes nothing. Show the person the warnings, the candidate link and the disclosure review. Never claim that the content is public.
-   Pass `keep_latest` only when the person says so. Without it the hub's default applies.
-   On `E_UPSTREAM_UNCERTAIN`, check the candidate on the hub before you try again.

## Sharing and the hub

rdy can connect to a hub service for sharing and publication. This release has no push, pull or hub clone yet.

-   `rdy_remote` lists and edits remotes offline. A remote has a `name`, an HTTPS `url` and a mode, `share` or `publish`. At most one remote is `share`.
-   Sign-in: `rdy_auth {op: "start", install, machine_name}` returns a card and sends nothing. Show the card.
-   Relay the answer: `start` again with `card_hash`, `answer` (`confirm` or `cancel`), `evidence` and `question`. Give the person the `user_code` and `verification_uri`, and poll `state`.
-   You never see, ask for or handle a token. `rdy auth token` is for credential programs, not for agents.
-   `rdy_key_bind {kind}` returns a `confirm_url` and state `pending`. Give the person the link: the key binds only when they confirm it on the hub's page.
-   Retire or revoke a key only on the person's word. Revoke is for a key that may be compromised.
-   On `E_UPSTREAM_UNCERTAIN`, the request may have completed. Check its state on the hub before you try again.
-   Sign-in fails with `E_UPSTREAM_PROTOCOL` when the hub names an account handle outside the actor form. Tell the person.

rulesets.title: Publications and the hub
rulesets.when: check or publish a profile, or use a hub

rows.text:
# Reviews and checks

Load this ruleset when you run or answer a review.

## Semantic review

1.  Start a session with role `reviewer`, under an actor that wrote neither block. Call `rdy_review_next {kind: "tension"}` at once.
2.  Answer with `rdy_review_submit {request, case_hash, verdict}`. A `tension` verdict needs 1 to 20 `citations` (`{block, note}`).
3.  To advise that a tension should block, add `severity: "blocking"` and a `reason`. On `E_REVIEW_STALE`, take the next request.

Advice to block gates nothing until the person accepts its `resolve` card. Relay their answer like any other card.

## Authoring checks

`rdy_review` runs agent checks on your own work. `{op: "checks"}` lists them: `contradiction`, `meaning_preservation`, `implementation_fidelity`, `decision_review`, `entity_divergence`, `prose_drift`, `diff_contradicts` and `confirmation`.

-   Run a check only when the author or the person asks for it.
-   `{op: "run", check, subject}` records a request on your own work and returns its case. The subject is a block, a change, `P-x@n`, a pair of blocks, or `{decision, code}` for `diff_contradicts`.
-   `{op: "request", check, subject, reason}` asks for an independent review. When you request it for the person, pass their `evidence` and your `question`.
-   `{op: "list", open?, subject?}` lists the requests and their verdicts.
-   A verdict is `pass`, `concern` or `fail`. A `concern` or `fail` shows as a fact on the approval card. Show it to the person before you relay their answer. A `contradiction` verdict shows as a tension, not as a fact.
-   A verdict blocks a version only when the person accepts it as blocking on the card. A new version does not keep that acceptance.
-   `all_recommended` refuses an approve card that shows a `concern` or `fail` that no person accepted. Relay that card on its own.
-   CLI: `rdy review checks|run|request|list`.

Run an authoring check only when the author or a person asks. Show its verdict on the current approval card before relaying a person's answer.

# Diagrams

Load this ruleset when you write a diagram.

## Diagrams

A `diagram` block holds its source in the body, with `lang` (`mermaid` or `d2`) and an `alt` text. rdy draws a Mermaid diagram as SVG when it builds a site.

-   rdy draws four Mermaid types: flowchart (also `graph`), class, sequence and state. Any other type shows its source as a code block, with `W_DIAGRAM_UNSUPPORTED`.
-   A D2 diagram always shows its source.
-   A Mermaid diagram that does not parse, or is over a size bound, shows its source with `W_DIAGRAM_INVALID`. A drawing that fails rdy's checks shows its source with `W_DIAGRAM_FAILED`. The build never fails for a diagram.
-   The bounds: 65,536 bytes of source, 2,048 statements and a nesting depth of 32. In a flowchart, close each subgraph with `end`, and keep each arrow to 256 bytes or fewer.
-   The arrows and groups of one diagram cost at most 200. An arrow costs one for each rank it spans, so a longer arrow costs more. A group, a state note and each boundary between concurrent regions cost one each.
-   To fix a bound, make the diagram smaller, split it into parts, or use shorter arrows.
-   A build's warnings name the doc and the block of each diagram that rdy could not draw. Relay them to the person, then fix the source if they ask.
-   `rdy_schema` lists the three warnings, with when each applies and its fix.

-   Keep a diagram free of loops. The site's layout draws back edges and state-diagram edges across boxes. Use a top-down flowchart, and put the loop in the box text, such as "proposes again".

# Subagents and alternatives

Load this ruleset when you use subagents or alternative sets.

## Subagents and swarms

-   Give every subagent its own `run`, and so its own view and inbox. A write to another session's view fails with `E_VIEW_OWNER`.
-   The main agent reads each subagent's changes with `rdy_view {op: "show", view: "<run>"}`. It includes them with `rdy_view {op: "include", changes: [...]}`.
-   The main agent alone runs the checks, answers the plan, proposes, shows the cards and relays.
-   A subagent never attests a ruling it did not see. The main agent records the person's rulings itself.
-   A reviewer subagent uses its own actor, such as `agent:alex/claude-review`. rdy reads independence from the actor, not the run.
-   To copy changes without their dependencies, use `rdy_view {op: "replay", changes}`. It writes a new change for each listed change into your open view, as one act that one undo removes. A block whose version differs from the change's base becomes a conflict: resolve it by writing the block. CLI: `rdy view replay <view> <changes>...`.
-   Closing a view withdraws its open proposal for good.

Before a larger change, post an intent (`rdy_intent`) on its area or blocks; write responses name other sessions' intents on what you wrote, and nothing is ever locked.

## Alternatives

An alternative set holds two or more views that answer one question (`rdy_alternatives`). A proposal from a member view passes `alternatives: {set, chosen}` with its own member. Landing it closes the other members.

-   The version must name one proposed decision for the options it considered. Otherwise it is not ready (`E_ALT_DECISION`). Answer the set's question with that decision.

rulesets.name: project-ops

rows.text:
# Project operations

Load this ruleset when you dump, load, import, redact, sign or upgrade.

## Dumps and moving a project

-   `rdy_dump {out}` writes the whole project, with every relay's evidence, to one new file. It is unsigned, and as private as the store.
-   `rdy_dump {out, after}` writes an increment after `after`, the newest earlier dump or increment of this project. CLI: `rdy dump --after <earlier> <file>`.
-   When nothing is newer, `out` is null. rdy refuses an `out` that exists even then, so pick a new path each time.
-   `rdy_load` and `rdy_clone` write only into a directory with no store.
-   To load a chain, pass the increments in order: `rdy_load {file, dir, then: [...]}`. CLI: `rdy load <file> <dir> --then <inc>`, once for each increment. A wrong order fails with `E_DUMP_CHAIN`.
-   To load part of a chain, pass `stop_at` (`landing:<hash>`, `tag:<name>` or `pos:<segment>.<offset>`). CLI: `--stop-at`.
-   A stop before a content removal still loads, with `W_STOP_BEFORE_REDACTION`: the removed content is back in that store. Tell the person. Never propose the removal again yourself.
-   Every later rdy reads every released dump format. rdy 0.35.0 writes dump format 4. It carries a feature store.
-   `rdy_export` writes local files for people. It is not a publication. Relay its warnings, and read the project through the tools.


> **Note**
>
> On Windows, a path inside a project or a code repo stays logical, with `/`, such as `src/app.rs` in `code_paths`. A path on disk is native, such as `C:\Users\ana\shop.rdydump` for a dump's `out`. In JSON, write each backslash twice: `"C:\\Users\\ana\\shop.rdydump"`.

## The store

**Upgrades.** A store has a format and a list of features. When a newer rdy needs an upgrade step, it runs the upgrade as it opens the store, and keeps a backup beside the store. `rdy upgrade` runs the same upgrade.

-   `rdy_upgrade {dry_run: true}` reports the upgrade without writes, and the last upgrade receipt.
-   On `E_STORE_FORMAT`, give the person the fix from the error. It names the rdy to use, a dump and load, or `rdy upgrade`. Don't run them yourself.
-   `E_STORE_READ_ONLY` means this rdy can only read the store. Tell the person which rdy build the refusal names.
-   `E_UPGRADE_MOVED`: the store changed after the upgrade was planned. Run the dry run again.
-   `E_UPGRADE_BACKUP` and `E_UPGRADE_FAILED` are for the person. On `E_UPGRADE_FAILED`, rdy never restores the backup itself: the person stops the daemon and restores it. Give them the message, which names the backup.

**Compaction.** `rdy_compact` frees the disk space of content that a redaction removed. It changes no content and no log position, so a writer session may run it. Run it with `dry_run: true` first, and show the person the report. CLI: `rdy compact --dry-run`.

**Followers.** A host can keep a read-only follower of a store. Every write to a follower fails with `E_STORE_FOLLOWER`. Write through the source store instead.

## Imports

`rdy_import {dir, view}` reads a format-3 export tree into a view, in a writer session. It never writes into canon. CLI: `rdy import <dir> --view <view>`.

-   Each change keeps its source author, and `imported_by` names your session.
-   A version that carries an imported accepted or rejected decision shows the fact `Imported` and always needs a person.
-   Handing a view to another owner is the person's act. Relay it on their word: `rdy_view {op: "own", view, owner: {actor, run?}, evidence, question}`. Leave out `run` for an owner with no run. CLI: `rdy view own <view> <actor> --run <run>`.

## Redaction

Before proposing content removal, call `rdy_redact` with `dry_run` true. Show its report and warnings. Record the request, then use `rdy_propose` and `rdy_pending`. Only a person can approve it.

These details apply too:

-   Write the `reason` without the content itself: rdy keeps it as audit text.
-   Show every warning in the dry run report. For the class `secret`, tell the person to rotate the secret.
-   A removal lands only with the person's answer on its own card. `all_recommended` and an agent's own approval fail with `E_REDACTION_HUMAN`.
-   On `E_REDACTION_STALE`, run the dry run again and show the new report.
-   A redaction cannot erase dumps, exports, renders, clones or other copies outside the store. Say so.
-   `W_REDACTION_QUOTES` says what stays: review citations, answer notes and change-plan versions that quote the content, among others. Pass it on.
-   On `W_STOP_BEFORE_REDACTION`, tell the person. Never record a removal again on your own.

## Signing

Signing goes through the SSH agent, and rdy never reads a private key. Leave the `signing.*` settings to the person.

-   Relay a `W_SIGNING_FAILED` warning to the person: the act landed unsigned. Under `always`, rdy refuses the act instead.
-   After the person fixes signing, `rdy_sign {target}` signs your relay.
-   Sign with the person's key (`kind: "approval"` or `"tag"`) only when they ask.
-   A signature shows that a key signed, not that the person read the act. Never claim more.


> **Note**
>
> On Windows, rdy signs only through the agent that `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` names, in the environment of the process that runs `rdy mcp`. The value must name a local pipe, `\\.\pipe\<name>`. For the Windows OpenSSH agent, the person sets it to `\\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent`. rdy does not look for that agent by itself. Any other value, such as the file socket of Git for Windows, gives `the SSH agent could not sign: connection failed`.

rulesets.title: Project operations
rulesets.when: dump, load, import, redact, sign or upgrade

rulesets.name: troubleshoot

rows.text:
# Troubleshooting

Load this ruleset when you hit an actor, run or daemon error.

## Actors and runs

rdy checks the actor and the run of every new session. It also checks every actor that you name, such as a view owner or `--relayed-by`. A value outside the form fails with `E_BAD_INPUT`, and the fix gives the form.

-   An actor is `human:<name>`, `agent:<name>`, `agent:<handle>/<name>` or `ci:<repo_id>/<name>`. Your actor is always an `agent:` actor, such as `agent:claude` or `agent:alex/claude-review`.
-   A name has 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_` or `.`. It starts and ends with a letter or digit.
-   A run has 1 to 64 letters, digits, `-`, `_` or `.`. It starts and ends with a letter or digit.
-   The runs `none`, `canon`, `inflight` and `work` are reserved, as is every run that starts with `reaffirm-`.
-   rdy keeps the actor and the run apart. It prints them as `<actor> (run <run>)`, never as `actor/run`.
-   An `rdy_session` refusal leaves your earlier session, view and subscription as they were.
-   `role` is `reader`, `writer` or `reviewer`, and the default is `writer`. A reader may pass `view: "canon"` to read canon by default.

## The daemon and the MCP server

-   `E_DAEMON_START`: tell the person, and follow the fix in the message.
-   `E_DAEMON_GONE`: the daemon closed the connection before it answered. A write may or may not have committed, and rdy does not retry it.
-   When the daemon goes away, `rdy mcp` answers each open call with `E_DAEMON_GONE` and exits. Your host must start the rdy MCP server again. Then read your view before you retry.
-   `E_DAEMON_VERSION`, or stale replies after an rdy update: ask the person, then run `rdy serve --stop`. It ends every session.
-   `W_DAEMON_BUILD`: the running daemon is another build of the same rdy version. When the other clients close, the daemon restarts on your build. Tell the person. To restart it at once, ask them first, then run `rdy serve --stop`.
-   A daemon that rdy started stops after 10 idle minutes, and the live site goes with it. For a long review, ask the person to start `rdy serve` in a terminal first.


> **Note**
>
> On Windows, rdy serves MCP over stdio. MCP over HTTP comes in a later release.
>
> -   The host runs `rdy mcp --project <directory>` with a native path, such as `C:\Users\ana\shop`. Messages show plain drive paths like this one, never `\\?\`.
> -   The daemon listens on a named pipe, `\\.\pipe\rdy-<hash>`, that only the person's account can open. A daemon that another account runs is refused: `the daemon on <pipe> belongs to another account (<SID>)`.
> -   `E_DAEMON_START` reads `could not start the daemon: <detail>`. Tell the person, and give them its fix.
> -   `E_IO` with `<path> is not private to this account` or `<path> is a reparse point; rdy will not follow it`: tell the person. Never change file permissions yourself.
> -   Windows refuses to move `.rdy` while its daemon runs, and the daemon serves on. Ask the person, then run `rdy serve --stop` before the move.

rulesets.title: Troubleshooting
rulesets.when: hit an actor, run or daemon error
